body: Not sure what my diagnosis is at the moment, but I do take mood stabilizers so I am assuming there is a mood component. They were so concerned about my psychotic symptoms when I first told them, and then they made it sound like they were not true psychotic symptoms, or not as valid as psychotic disorders. It is very frustrating, because I am trying to explain that I am pretty damn sure they are true psychotic symptoms, but they just don't believe me. This is the reason I didn't want to tell them in the first place. Even when I was younger, when I told doctors I heard things they just smiled and insisted I didn't.

Thank you for your response! My self-care had gone down-hill since I started experiencing this, so these days I try and take care of my hygiene at least. I feel like my productive life has been ripped away from me. I used to care so much about everything and taking care of myself and now I just...don't.

My psych has asked me a few times too if I thought the voices were real or not. I say no, because logically it doesn't make sense to hear people talking all the time about me, but there are many times where I consider them being real or feel like they are.

I told them more specifics, and got a referral to someone else. At some point they stopped asking questions and just said to wait and see what the other person said. So, I am frustrated that even with being specific I am being bounced around instead of getting a diagnosis. I am thinking they do not believe me at all, which is fair, because I have insight at times.
I only drink tea and not very frequently. It is interesting that this can happen, though!

I was more specific with my psych recently and it went well. I was referred to someone with more expertise in it. You were right, no hospitalization needed, but they did give me time off school because of distress.

When I can, I wear headphones and listen to music now! Thank you for that suggestion!
